subject: sociology
title: Interactionism Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch interactionist ideas to the exam. Is the label everything, or is structure still in charge?
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch evaluating interactionism, labelling theory and structural critiques.
final_note: Great answers state the label, name the study and then add a structural counter.

concepts.def: Some pupils resist or rework the label given them.
Goffman: spoilt identity from a negative label.
Path into ongoing deviance after labelling.
Reality built by shared definitions, not fixed.
Says interactionism ignores class, gender, race.

walkthroughs.body_html: Labelling theory shows the human, daily process behind big stats. It explains why two pupils doing the same act can be treated very differently and how reputations stick. It also exposes media power to shape reality.
Marxists argue labelling ignores who has the power to label and why. Feminists note that gendered labels reflect patriarchy. Some pupils negotiate labels successfully, so it is not all determined.
Define labelling. Name a study (Becker 1963; Rosenthal & Jacobson 1968; Cohen 1972). Apply to school or crime. Counter with Marxism or feminism. End with a clear judgement on label vs structure.
